propositions: The snapshot janitor's free-space trigger uses a 2-GiB absolute floor that does not scale with disk size; on a 30-GiB root this is only crossed at 93.3% used, above the 85% alarm threshold and the 90% peak reached, so reclaim never engages.

The 7-day cold-trim is dead code on containers with ~23-hour lifetimes, and the promised byte-total backstop is not implemented in _gc_pass, leaving only the unreachable absolute watermark as the effective trigger.

Review-bot materializes ~620-MiB full copies of the tickets tree per review on a cache key that advances every ~26 seconds with minimal reuse, driving ~4.4 GiB/h growth that the non-firing reclaim mechanism cannot contain.

The repair adds a volume-relative watermark term (whole-percent integer) that triggers reclaim before the alarm floor on small volumes, with hysteresis to a target margin so reclaim does not re-fire every 300 seconds.
The new knob defaults to 0 (disabled) to preserve existing deployments unchanged; review-bot opts in at 20% headroom (80% used), matching the existing DISK_PRESSURE_PCT threshold.
The test RED oracle verifies 0 evictions at 85% and 90% used on the pre-fix code, GREEN after repair, and RED again under exact-defect mutation forcing the absolute-only watermark.
